newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia yr/yr vehicle sales up 4.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia yr/yr vehicle sales up 4.4 pct.

text.p: Australian new vehicle sales were up by 4,290 vehicles or 4.4 percent in the first two months of 1997 compared with a year earlier, The Federal Chamber of Automotive Industries (FCAI) reported on Friday.
The FCAI said the daily selling rate for January/February was 2,065.8 compared with 1,938.7 a year earlier.

However, the industry body said the total passenger vehicle market was up by just 153 vehicles (0.4 percent) in spite of a continued strong performance in the small call segement, which rose by 2,476 units or 21.6 percent.
The sports car sector was up by 302 units (41.0 percent), luxury car by 163 (15.5 percent) and light car by 74 (1.9 percent) compared with February 1996.
However, the medium car sector fell by 1,377 (27.6 percent), upper medium car by 1,043 (6.2 percent), prestige car by 417 (17.4 percent) and people movers by 23 (5.3 percent).

The light truck market recorded an increase of 719 vehicles or 8.5 percent over February 1996, with particularly strong performances by the all terrain wagon segment, which rose 994 units or 26 percent, the FCAI said.

The heavy truck market, for the second month this year, performed ahead of the same month in 1996 with 1,966 vehicles sold year to date compared with 1,917 a year earlier, representing a year-on-year increase of 2.5 percent.
For the year to date, General Motors Corp held a 20.1 percent market share with sales of 19,442 vehicles.

Among the other three local manufacturers, Ford Motor Co held 18.9 percent with sales of 18,330 vehicles, Toyota Motor Corp held 15.7 percent with sales of 17,018 and Mitsubishi Motors Corp held 12.1 percent with sales of 9,025.
